title: Electronegativity trends in the periodic table
body: Electronegativity of the representative elements increases from left to right across a period and decreases going down a group, which can be explained qualitatively with electronic structure, the shell model, and Coulomb's law.
ced_evidence: 2.1.A.1: "Electronegativity values for the representative elements increase going from left to right across a period and decrease going down a group."

title: Potential energy vs. internuclear distance graph
body: Graph of potential energy versus the distance between two atoms, used to describe the interaction between the atoms, with the lowest-energy point marking the equilibrium bond length and the bond energy read from the energy needed to separate the atoms.

items.label: Vertical axis: potential energy
items.meaning: Potential energy of the pair of interacting atoms.

items.label: Horizontal axis: internuclear distance
items.meaning: Distance between the nuclei of the two atoms.

items.label: Lowest point of the curve
items.meaning: Equilibrium bond length: the separation between atoms at which the potential energy is lowest.

items.label: Depth of the energy well
items.meaning: Bond energy: the energy required to separate the atoms.

items.label: Effect of bond order
items.meaning: Bonds with a higher order (single, double, triple) are shorter and have larger bond energies.

ced_evidence: 2.2.A.1: "graph of potential energy versus the distance between atoms (internuclear distance)"; "equilibrium bond length (the separation between atoms at which the potential energy is lowest)"; "bond energy (the energy required to separate the atoms)"

title: Resonance for equivalent Lewis structures
body: When more than one equivalent Lewis structure can be constructed, resonance must be included as a refinement to the Lewis structure so that predictions of molecular structure and properties are qualitatively accurate.
ced_evidence: 2.6.A.1: "In cases where more than one equivalent Lewis structure can be constructed, resonance must be included as a refinement to the Lewis structure."

title: Choosing among nonequivalent Lewis diagrams
body: When several valid Lewis diagrams are possible and they are not equivalent, use the octet rule and formal charge as the criteria to decide which one is the best model for predicting molecular structure and properties.
ced_evidence: 2.6.A.2: "The octet rule and formal charge can be used as criteria for determining which of several possible valid Lewis diagrams provides the best model"

title: Formal charge of an atom in a Lewis diagram
body: \text{FC} = (\text{valence e}^-\text{ of the free atom}) - (\text{nonbonding e}^-) - \tfrac{1}{2}(\text{bonding e}^-)
caution: The CED does not print this formula; it requires students to calculate formal charges and use them to select among Lewis structures. Start from the correct number of valence electrons, since using the wrong number is a common mistake.
ced_evidence: 2.6.A.2 and Unit 2 'Preparing for the AP Exam': "calculating and connecting formal charges in Lewis structures"

title: Hybridization and ideal bond angles
body: The sp, sp2, and sp3 hybridization labels for a central atom correspond to ideal bond angles of 180°, 120°, and 109.5°.
ced_evidence: 2.7.A.3: "sp hybridized, its ideal bond angles are 180°; for sp2 hybridized atoms the bond angles are 120°; and for sp3 hybridized atoms the bond angles are 109.5°."

title: Molecular geometries named in the CED
body: The molecular geometries that students must predict from Lewis diagrams and VSEPR theory, in the CED's order.
caution: Answer with the geometry name itself. A bond angle alone, or an invalid combined label such as 'tetrahedral pyramidal', does not earn the point. For more than four electron pairs around the central atom, only the shape of the molecule is required.
ced_evidence: 2.7.A.2.i: "Molecular geometry (linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal pyramidal, bent, trigonal bipyramidal, seesaw, T-shaped, octahedral, square pyramidal, square planar)"
